key_insight: WHITE-Net is a deep learning model that segments white matter hyperintensities accurately across diverse MRI settings by training on multisite, variable-quality data.
clinical_relevance: It could help large-scale neuroimaging studies quantify small vessel disease more reliably and efficiently without manual tuning.
method: Trained on multisite MRI data with varied scanners, protocols, and resolutions
Designed for fast inference and minimal parameter tuning
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on three independent datasets (BrainLaus, ADNI, and WMH Challenge) and performed strongly across different lesion loads and imaging conditions.
watch_item: As with any automated segmentation tool, performance may vary on unseen acquisition settings or extreme image artifacts, so local validation is important.
paper_title: WHITE-Net : White matter HyperIntensities Tissue Extraction using deep learning Network
